# Largest Substring Between Two Equal Characters.

@example The first and last a have "nan" between them; the gap may hold the middle a.
"banana"
=> 3

@example Only d occurs twice, and its two copies are neighbours.
"teddy"
=> 0

@example Every letter is different, so there is no gap.
"world"
=> -1

# A single letter.
"z"
=> -1

# Two letters, the same or different.
"qq"
=> 0

"qr"
=> -1

# All 26 letters once each.
"qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm"
=> -1

# A 27th letter must repeat one of them.
"qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnmg"
=> 11

# Neighbouring letters only: 0, not -1.
"pressing"
=> 0

# Four copies of o: the gap from the first to the last, though any two
# neighbouring copies are close.
"gotoxoyoz"
=> 5

# The letter at position 0 repeats once, before the end.
"wolfwe"
=> 3

# The widest gap belongs to a rarer letter, not to the most frequent one
# and not to the first letter.
"xqbbbbbqy"
=> 5

# The first and last letters match: the answer is the length minus 2.
"keeeeeeek"
=> 7

# 300 letters, the first and last equal: the gap ends at position 299.
""
=> 298

# 300 letters in runs; the widest gap runs from position 260 to 299, past
# what a byte-sized position holds.
""
=> 38

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"cmpybpfjg"
=> 2

@gen 2 small
"bbbbbbb"
=> 5

@gen 3 small
"mdhxhs"
=> 1

@gen 4 small
"awdi"
=> -1

@gen 5 small
"aaaaaaabbb"
=> 5

@gen 6 small
"kk"
=> 0

@gen 7 small
"cm"
=> -1

# Full-size cases: 300 letters.
@gen 1
""
=> 23

@gen 2
""
=> 295

@gen 3
""
=> 254
